title: Stir milk into a mug of coffee with a teaspoon
description: With a dexterous hand on the right arm of a Tianji Marvin dual-arm stand (Sharpa Wave by default, or Wuji Hand 2.2), take the teaspoon that the hand holds upright above a mug of coffee (the approved T11 film's first frame), stir six full revolutions with its bowl in the coffee, lift it out and lay it on the worktop beside the mug, then let go; a knocked mug or a dropped spoon fails the episode at once.
mechanism: free rigid mug and teaspoon; coffee summarised by bowl revolutions; Marvin dual-arm stand
instruction: Mix the milk into the coffee: stir it six times with the teaspoon, then lay the spoon on the worktop beside the mug. The 300 g mug (inner radius 50 mm, 100 mm tall, 8 mm floor) stands upright on the stone worktop (top at z = 0.75 m) with its axis at x = 0.48 m, y = 0.015 m; the coffee, milk already poured, fills it to 64 mm above the mug base (z = 0.814 m). The approved source film (a kinematic demonstration without hands) starts with the teaspoon suspended upright above the rim; here the right hand holds the 35 g teaspoon there, upright, bowl down, in a thumb-index pinch near the top of its handle, with the bowl centre about 0.12 m above the mug base just over the rim (the milk is already poured; the film pours it from an offscreen supply). With the Wuji hand selected (no Wuji start grasp exists yet), the spoon instead starts leaning in the mug (bowl on the mug floor, handle on the rim) and the open Wuji hand hangs about 0.25 m above the mug; the stages are the same. Success requires three stages in order. (1) Submerged in hand: the thumb and at least one other finger touch the spoon, and the bowl centre, bowl tip and bowl neck (23 mm either side of the centre along the spoon) are all between 4 mm and 64 mm above the mug base and within 50 mm of the mug axis. (2) Stirred: the bowl centre revolves at least six full turns about the mug's vertical axis (world frame; net signed angle). The angle accumulates only while the stage-1 condition holds and the bowl centre is at least 8 mm from the axis; a step of more than 0.785 rad in one control is ignored, and the count restarts from zero whenever the bowl leaves the coffee before six turns are complete. (3) Laid down: no part of the hand touches the spoon, the spoon touches the worktop and not the mug, its bowl centre and handle end are both at least 0.10 m from the mug axis horizontally, its axis is within 15 degrees of horizontal, and spoon and mug are still (linear speed at most 0.02 m/s, angular speed at most 0.5 rad/s), for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). The episode ends with success at that moment. The coffee is not simulated: it exerts no force, and the mixing is judged only by these bowl revolutions below its surface. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics substep, when the mug tilts more than 10 degrees, slides more than 20 mm or is lifted more than 5 mm; when the spoon touches the floor, or touches the worktop before the six turns are complete; when the spoon touches neither the hand, the mug nor the worktop while its centre of mass falls faster than 0.2 m/s (a dropped spoon cannot be caught again); when the mug touches the floor; when a spoon reference point (bowl centre, tip, neck or handle end) is more than 3 mm below the worktop top or the mug base more than 5 mm below it; when the bowl centre or the handle end leaves the workspace box x in [0, 0.96] m, y in [-0.48, 0.48] m, z in [0.70, 1.60] m; when a fingertip enters the coffee (inside the mug radius below the coffee surface); when an arm link, the stand or the parked left hand touches the mug, the spoon or the worktop; or when the physics becomes unstable; later actions cannot undo a failure. Only robot actuator targets are allowed; no object teleports, grasp welds, scripted object motion or direct object forces. The episode allows at most 3000 controls at 50 Hz; reaching that limit without success is a failure.
modeling: Tianji Marvin dual-arm stand at the world origin (stand plate on the floor at z = -0.1 m), right arm and right hand active, left arm parked; free rigid mug (300 g; floor disk, 32 wall boxes and three handle boxes under the approved T11 refined visual mesh) and teaspoon (35 g; 2.7 mm shaft capsule and two crossed flat bowl slabs under the approved visual mesh). The coffee/milk is a visual surface only; stirring is measured as revolutions of the bowl about the mug axis below that surface. The start is the source film's first frame (spoon held upright above the mug), made physically: a settled contact pinch, no weld.
